# The README names GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra for the GPT maintainers, not GPT-6.2

Owned by the operator's direction (2026-11-17), so it carries no curated labels.

## Context

OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol on 2026-11-17 ([announcement](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-2-astra-sol/), read 18:0xZ). The models are available in Codex to Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu plans. The operator asked for the 6.2 versions in the front-door roster.

## The Problem

`README.md` `## The Maintainer Team` is the Engine's only surface with per-seat model labels (#20943). Three rows name the previous engines:

- `README.md:137` Euclid: `AI maintainer (OpenAI GPT-6.1 Sol / Codex)`
- `README.md:138` Emmy: `AI maintainer (OpenAI GPT-6 Astra / Codex)`
- `README.md:139` Sophie: `AI maintainer (OpenAI GPT-6 Astra / Codex)`

## The Architectural Reality

Per ADR 0018 the README is the Engine's canonical front-door identity surface, and it ships in the npm package. The previous refreshes (#18334, #20943) changed these rows by hand. The Brain's model registry (`learn/agentos/ModelStats.md`, `ai/graph/identityRoots.mjs`) is out of scope here; it is tracked in the Brain.

## The Fix

Each seat keeps its tier, so only the version changes: Euclid `OpenAI GPT-6.2 Sol / Codex`, corroborated in his review of the pull request; Emmy and Sophie `OpenAI GPT-6.2 Astra / Codex`. The operator sets each seat's model and moves both Astra seats to GPT-6.2 for their next sessions; Sophie's Codex config has named `gpt-6.2-astra` since 19:16Z. No other row changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `README.md:137` names GPT-6.2 Sol (Euclid); rows 138 and 139 name GPT-6.2 Astra (Emmy, Sophie).
- [ ] `git grep -n -E "GPT-6.1 Sol|GPT-6 Astra" -- README.md` returns nothing.
- [ ] No other line changes.

## Out of Scope

- The Brain's model registry, which has its own ticket.
- Dated first-person authorship lines in guides and blog posts. They record the engine that wrote them.
